market_view: Calm risk regime (VIX 15.2, down 7% on the day) but the 10-year yield is at its highest since November 2023 (4.80%); oil is up 10.7% in five days on the Iran war while gold fell 5.1% over the same span.

oil_gas.catalyst: Continuing hold from 2026-08-31: renewed US strikes on Iran (CNBC: WTI hits $90); today's record adds 'Hormuz Disruptions Redraw Shipping Lanes and Lift Freight Rates' and 'Chevron expands Venezuela presence with $7 billion plan' (Reuters). No truce or deal headline yet, so the supply disruption is still running.
oil_gas.reasoning: The supply shock is unresolved and there is no de-escalation headline. But WTI is already up 21% in 20 days, and the last XOM entry lagged its basket. Keeping it at the bar; the Venezuela headline is about Chevron, not XOM.

gold_miners.reasoning: Gold fell 5.1% in five days with the 10-year at a multi-year high. The NEM headlines are recaps of its run (Motley Fool, +34.5% in August), not catalysts. The jobs report adds variance.

chips.catalyst: none (considered 'NVIDIA to Acquire Hugging Face', NVIDIA Blog, $12.9B)
chips.reasoning: An acquirer-side deal this small relative to NVDA is not a one-sided catalyst, and NVDA already rose 3.2% on Sept 2. The semis ETF is down 8% over 60 days. Flat.

pharma.reasoning: There is no named LLY trial, approval or guidance headline; the Kalkine piece is filler. LLY is down 2.5% in five days while the sector is flat. Re-enter only on a named catalyst.

copper_uranium.reasoning: The FCX hold closed about Sept 1 at +9.02%. There is no fresh Congo or supply headline, copper is down 1.4% in five days, and the miner headlines (Ivanhoe -5.9%) are negative. Flat until a new supply shock.

would_change_my_mind: A US-Iran truce or deal headline would make me drop XOM; a fresh Congo or outage headline would put FCX back in; a named Lilly trial, approval or guidance headline would put LLY back in.

handoff.what_changed: WTI reached $91 (+10.7% in 5 days) with Hormuz disruption ongoing; Chevron (not Exxon) announced a $7B Venezuela plan. FCX closed about 09-01 at +9.02% and XOM 08-18 closed at -0.86%. NVDA is buying Hugging Face for $12.9B; the 10-year is at its highest since Nov 2023.

lessons.rule: Hypothesis only: oil longs opened on a named supply-shock escalation headline win over 10 days; entries after a long run do worse.
